topic:
Determine the sharp near-homogeneity frontier for ATE estimation with high-dimensional discrete confounders. For fixed known 0<epsilon<1/2, M>=1 and sigma in [0,2], observe n iid (X,A,Y) with X in [d], binary A, real Y, arbitrary unknown cell masses (null cells allowed), and unknown propensities in [epsilon,1-epsilon] on occupied cells. Consistency and conditional exchangeability identify tau=sum_k p_k(mu_1k-mu_0k). Each conditional mean lies in [-M/2,M/2] and each conditional central variance is at most M^2; no higher moments or bounded outcomes are assumed. Require max_k:p_k>0 |mu_1k-mu_0k-tau|<=sigma M, law by law. Uniformly over n>=3, 2<=d<=floor(n^2/log(en)), all sigma and M, determine a directly evaluable scalar rate r(n,d,sigma), a total computable estimator with worst-case MSE at most C_epsilon M^2 r, and a matching all-estimator same-class lower bound c_epsilon M^2 r. Comparison constants depend only on epsilon. Estimators may use the known class inputs but not unknown masses/propensities; define behavior on every sample, including empty cells.

The answer is open. With b=1/n+d/n^2 and u=d^2/[n^2 log^2(en)], the accepted same-class parent only proves lower b+sigma^2 min(1,u) versus upper 1/n+min(1,u,sigma^2+d/n^2). Resolve the entire shrinking-radius wedge and its transitions, not merely an endpoint, one sequence, or another bracket. At d=floor(n^(3/4)), sigma^2=u, current benchmarks range from order 1/n to order n^(-1/2)/log^2(en); this is a benchmark gap, not an asserted risk. Derive from the matched result exactly when approximately common effects retain collision-scale estimation and when rare-cell correction determines the rate. Do not stipulate that either existing bound is sharp.

The parent proves two anti-constraints: a hypothesis-independent outcome-channel transfer only gives product-scale lower separation, and the natural centered linear Chebyshev factorial lift has excessive singleton-pair variance even with oracle centering and sigma=0. Population bias reduction alone does not prove stochastic attainment. Any nonlinear stabilization/clipping must control its own uniform bias and risk under second moments. A new converse must respect the radius on every prior-support law, not merely on prior average. Proof architecture, estimator algebra and rate formula are delegated. Existing-selector optimality is eligible if a substantive new converse proves it. No unknown-radius adaptation or confidence-interval claim is requested.

Grounding: Zeng-Balakrishnan-Han-Kennedy, https://arxiv.org/html/2405.00118, Theorems2-4 and Section4.2 explicitly leave radius dependence open. Their Section7 401(k) eligibility/net-assets analysis is the consumer: quantify which near-homogeneity assumptions justify estimation gains in sparse adjustment cells. This does not validate that dataset's overlap or reported intervals. The accepted parent stat_discrete_ate_heterogeneity_frontier_v1 supplies the bracket and architecture obstructions, not the new frontier. Legal sanity witness: n=10,d=4,M=1,epsilon=1/4,sigma=1/8, uniform masses, propensities alternating1/3,2/3, control means0 and treated means alternating1/16,-1/16, with independent Rademacher potential-outcome noises; tau=0 and all class constraints hold.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A split-sample empirical-mass correction to the accepted occupancy-weighted pilot has an exact conditional error decomposition into outcome noise, centered effect deviations, and unmatched empirical mass. The draft derives a squared unmatched-mass bound of order (d/n)^2 and an inverse-binomial outcome-noise bound using only conditional second moments. Conditional on the imported pilot guarantee, it obtains M^2[1/n+sigma^2(d/n)^2] for d<=n, resolving the original polynomial-gap sequence at order M^2/n and narrowing the remaining bracket to a logarithmic gap. Checks included zero masses, empty blocks, exact homogeneity, saturation and the parent's failed channel and factorial constructions. The full frontier and proposed effective-log formula remain unproved.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Construct shared-design, exactly normalized marked-mixture priors with realization-wise radius control, concentrated ATE separation and small full-sample divergence at the proposed radius-dependent scale, or derive the corrected scale. The corresponding radius-dependent polynomial upper bound, stochastic covariance control and all uniform transitions also require proof; the draft lists every gap.
EARLY KILL TEST: At d=n and sigma^2=log^2(en)/n, test the shared-design mixture likelihood, normalization and target concentration. A design-only divergence term should stop that proposed architecture before full proofs, preserving the original answer-open problem.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_discrete_ate_shrinking_heterogeneity_sharp_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp finite-sample minimax MSE rate throughout the shrinking-radius wedge for ATE estimation over discrete-confounder laws satisfying max_k |tau_k-tau| <= sigma M.

source_refs.claim: Theorems 3–4 settle endpoint regimes, while Section 4.2 explicitly leaves the sharp dependence on maximal effect heterogeneity unresolved.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.excerpt: The delivered result is an all-alphabet, same-class minimax bracket rather than a complete shrinking-radius frontier.
The open issue is exactly the gap between the product term sigma^2 u and the smaller-factor term min(u,sigma^2).

open_problems.why_unsolved: Zeng et al. establish the unrestricted and exact-homogeneity benchmarks but do not identify the interpolation for shrinking sigma. The accepted parent narrows this to a same-class bracket: with b=1/n+d/n^2 and u=d^2/[n^2 log^2(en)], its lower bound contains b+sigma^2 min(1,u), whereas its upper bound contains 1/n+min(1,u,sigma^2+d/n^2). These can differ by a diverging factor in the residual wedge. Random unknown cell masses, empty cells, cross-arm collisions, and the self-centering restriction on cell effects must be handled simultaneously, so neither fixed-design shrinkage calculations nor interpolation between endpoint bounds resolves the problem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A directly evaluable scalar r(n,d,sigma), an everywhere-defined estimator with risk at most C_epsilon M^2 r, and an all-estimator lower bound at least c_epsilon M^2 r uniformly over the stated class, together with an explicit phase characterization of the collision and rare-cell transitions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its sparse-adjustment motivation, endpoint comparison, and 401(k) illustration provide the closest formulation of why approximate effect homogeneity may change the attainable rate.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Rich discrete adjustment makes exchangeability more plausible -> sparse cells make conventional ATE estimation occupancy-limited -> exact homogeneity enables collision-scale gains -> determine precisely how those gains degrade with the heterogeneity radius.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine occupancy-weighted treated-control estimation with fixed-sample moment-matching lower experiments while retaining the radius in every risk and divergence calculation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the identical statistical experiment, the endpoint rates, and the collision mechanism that the sought interpolation must unify.

method_exemplars.technique: Dualize a chi-square functional modulus into a bias-variance optimization and use it to prove matching quadratic-risk bounds across elbow regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired frontier is a radius-constrained scalar-functional problem with expected transitions among parametric, collision, and rare-cell scales.

method_exemplars.technique: Use heavy/light splitting, best-polynomial approximation, factorial-moment lifting, and matched fuzzy-hypothesis lower bounds for rare-category functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The rare-cell component of discrete-confounder ATE estimation is a marked and overlap-constrained analogue of large-alphabet functional estimation.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct shared-design, exactly normalized fuzzy-hypothesis priors whose every support law satisfies max_k |tau_k-tau| <= sigma M and whose ATE separation and full-sample divergence yield the sharp lower scale throughout the shrinking-radius wedge.

source_refs.claim: The general lower bound uses moment matching, while the homogeneous lower bound treats sigma=0 under a more specialized construction; intermediate radii remain open.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.excerpt: no channel in this entire fixed-kernel architecture can produce the requested order M min(sigma,rho).
A successful converse must jointly enforce realization-wise radius, exact normalization, fixed-sample indistinguishabili

open_problems.why_unsolved: Unrestricted marked-multinomial priors can vary masses and outcome marks independently to hide target separation, but the radius restriction couples every cell effect to the same mass-weighted ATE and must hold for each realized support law, not merely on prior average. The accepted parent's hypothesis-independent outcome channel preserves indistinguishability only by multiplying source separation by sigma, giving product-scale separation rather than the desired radius-sensitive scale. Exact normalization correlates coordinates, and permitting different designs across hypotheses introduces a potentially detectable design-only likelihood term. The first proof step that must change is therefore the prior construction itself, before tensorization, Poissonization, or moment matching can be applied.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For every relevant (n,d,sigma) regime, a pair of explicit priors supported law by law on the admissible class whose induced n-sample mixtures have total variation bounded away from one and whose ATEs concentrate in intervals separated by a constant multiple of M sqrt(r(n,d,sigma)), yielding a valid fuzzy-hypotheses minimax lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It formulates the exact marked-multinomial experiment and contrasts the unrestricted moment-matching converse with the distinct collision argument at exact homogeneity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sparse cells hide arm contrasts -> fuzzy hypotheses convert hidden contrasts into minimax lower bounds -> homogeneity changes the feasible target geometry -> intermediate radii require priors satisfying normalization and centering law by law.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct moment-matched priors through polynomial duality, prove target separation and Poissonized mixture closeness, and transfer the bound to fixed sample size.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested converse needs the same separation-versus-indistinguishability mechanism, augmented by shared design, exact normalization, and realization-wise radius constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Start from its large-alphabet marked hard family and fixed-sample transfer, replacing the independent outcome channel with a jointly centered marked-design construction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest lower-bound experiment on the identical causal model and identifies the endpoint constructions that a radius-aware prior must reconcile.

method_exemplars.technique: Express scalar-functional difficulty through a constrained chi-square modulus and dual bias-variance program, checking model-specific convexity and divergence conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A radius-indexed admissible set suggests a constrained modulus that may reveal the corrected lower scale if an explicit product prior cannot satisfy the support constraints.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a nonlinear, total radius-dependent ATE estimator that retains centered effect-deviation bias reduction while suppressing singleton-pair noise under only conditional second moments, or prove that the accepted known-radius selector is already rate-optimal.

source_refs.claim: The paper proposes polynomial-approximation estimators as a direction for closing its minimax gap, but does not obtain sharp shrinking-radius adaptation.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.claim: Best-polynomial approximation with unbiased factorial estimation attains sharp large-alphabet functional rates by jointly controlling approximation bias and stochastic fluctuation.
source_refs.author: Jiantao Jiao, Kartik Venkat, Yanjun Han, Tsachy Weissman

source_refs.excerpt: Oracle centering and independent sample splitting do not remove this singleton-pair diagonal.
A successful upper bound must retain the product-scaled population bias without the singleton-pair variance amplificatio

open_problems.why_unsolved: The accepted parent obtains a centered population approximation with squared error of order u{sigma^2+(t-tau)^2}, but its natural linear Chebyshev factorial lift has variance at least order log^2(em)/m on an oracle-centered sigma=0 Rademacher submodel rather than order 1/m. Thus population bias reduction does not establish stochastic attainment. The marked ATE summand also contains unknown propensities, and the radius constraint is centered at the unknown target. Nonlinear clipping, smoothing, empirical-mass correction, or localization must therefore control its own uniform bias, occupancy covariance, and heavy-tail risk under conditional second moments. The presolve empirical-mass calculation is explicitly unverified and covers only part of the parameter range, so it supplies a candidate mechanism rather than an established theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit estimator defined on every sample, including empty and one-arm-only cells, with a nonasymptotic bias-and-variance theorem at the sharp radius-dependent rate for all allowed n,d,sigma, or an all-estimator converse proving that the existing selector's rate cannot be uniformly improved.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from plug-in failure through collision weighting to polynomial approximation cleanly frames the stochastic construction problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Naive cellwise adjustment loses unseen-cell information -> near-common effects permit pooling -> rare cells invite polynomial or occupancy correction -> construct a stable radius-aware correction rather than proving only population bias reduction.

method_exemplars.technique: Split smooth and nonsmooth probability regions, lift a best polynomial with factorial moments, and bound aggregate approximation bias and coefficient variance together.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Rare confounder cells create the same large-alphabet nonsmoothness, but the lift must be redesigned for treated-control marks and the centered heterogeneity radius.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace a global high-degree polynomial by localized moment matching and prove stochastic control through neighborhood localization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Localization is a plausible route around the global factorial lift's singleton-pair variance while preserving rare-cell bias reduction.

method_exemplars.technique: Use higher-order U-statistic corrections and balance truncation bias against degenerate-kernel variance for causal and missing-data functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired estimator also uses repeated observations to remove nonlinear nuisance bias, but requires occupancy-specific projection and covariance control under only second moments.

literature_map:
Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy (2024, arXiv:2405.00118) define the discrete-confounder experiment, prove unrestricted and exact-homogeneity benchmarks, and explicitly leave sharp radius dependence open.
Their Section 7 401(k) example contains thousands of empirically sparse adjustment cells and motivates quantifying when homogeneity-based gains are defensible without validating overlap in that dataset.
Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman (2015, IEEE TIT) develop best-polynomial estimators and fuzzy-hypothesis converses for large-alphabet functionals.
Wu and Yang (2019, Annals of Statistics) sharpen the Chebyshev-approximation and moment-matching duality for unseen-support estimation.
Han, Jiao, and Weissman (2018, COLT) replace unstable global polynomials with local moment matching, suggesting a possible stabilization route.
Orlitsky, Suresh, and Wu (2016, PNAS) show that randomized smoothing can stabilize an unseen-species series whose raw unbiased coefficients have explosive variance.
Robins, Li, Mukherjee, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2017, Annals of Statistics) balance higher-order correction bias against degenerate U-statistic variance for causal and missing-data functionals.
Polyanskiy and Wu (2026, Annals of Statistics) connect Le Cam functional moduli to estimator bias-variance programs and minimax elbow phenomena, subject to model-specific structural checks.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2021, Econometrica) derive finite-sample optimal ATE estimators under convex restrictions but condition on treatment and covariate realizations rather than unknown random cell masses.
Hirshberg and Wager (2021, Annals of Statistics) and Athey, Imbens, and Wager (2018, JRSSB) use minimax balancing and augmentation under structured regression models, not arbitrary categorical masses.
D'Amour, Ding, Feller, Lei, and Sekhon (2021, Journal of Econometrics) clarify the strength of high-dimensional overlap assumptions and why fixed epsilon must remain explicit here.
Gao and Han (2020, NeurIPS) obtain heterogeneous-treatment-effect rates under geometric smoothness and density-ratio structure absent from this categorical model.
De Chaisemartin (2021) and Kwon and Sun (2025, arXiv:2510.05454) study bounded-effect or bounded-heterogeneity shrinkage but do not handle random empty cells or prove all-estimator minimaxity here.
The closest literatures therefore separately supply sparse-functional approximation, robust higher-order correction, convex shrinkage, and modulus duality; none resolves their interaction under a law-by-law sup-norm CATE radius.
No occupied target-method pair was found combining arbitrary unknown discrete masses, unknown overlapping propensities, conditional second moments only, and a sharp uniform shrinking-radius ATE frontier.
